# kcore_slurm_cluster (Resource)

Slurm cluster on kcoreOS nodes (`kctl apply -f` with `kind: SlurmCluster`). Compute members are cordoned so the VM scheduler leaves them to slurmd. A node belongs to at most one cluster. Changing `name`, `cluster_name`, or the controller node replaces the cluster. Destroy disables Slurm on the members and uncordons the compute nodes.

Apply plans the cluster first and stops on any blocking issue, such as a compute node that still hosts guest VMs. It then waits until the reconciler reports the cluster `ready`; set `wait_for_ready = false` to return as soon as the controller accepts the spec. Day-2 operations (`kctl slurm drain-node`, `resume-node`, `rotate-munge-key`) stay in `kctl`. The lab apply of this resource has not been run yet.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "kcore_slurm_cluster" "hpc" {
  name = "hpc-a"

  controller {
    node_id = "node-101"
    address = "10.0.0.11"
    iface   = "enp6s0"
  }

  login_node_ids = ["node-101"]

  compute {
    node_id    = "node-102"
    address    = "10.0.0.12"
    iface      = "enp6s0"
    partitions = ["batch"]
  }

  compute {
    node_id    = "node-103"
    address    = "10.0.0.13"
    iface      = "enp6s0"
    partitions = ["batch"]
  }

  partition {
    name     = "batch"
    default  = true
    max_time = "INFINITE"
    state    = "UP"
  }

  user {
    name     = "alice"
    uid      = 2001
    ssh_keys = ["ssh-ed25519 AAAA... alice@example"]
  }

  storage {
    mode    = "nfs"
    exports = ["/home", "/scratch"]
  }

  timeouts {
    create = "90m"
  }
}

data "kcore_slurm_cluster" "hpc" {
  name = kcore_slurm_cluster.hpc.name
}

output "hpc_phase" {
  value = data.kcore_slurm_cluster.hpc.phase
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `compute` (Block List, Min: 1) Compute members. Planning refuses a node that still hosts guest VMs. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--compute))
- `controller` (Block List, Min: 1, Max: 1) Node that runs slurmctld. Changing the node replaces the cluster. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--controller))
- `name` (String) Resource name (`metadata.name`).
- `partition` (Block List, Min: 1) Slurm partitions. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--partition))

### Optional

- `accounting` (Block List, Max: 1) slurmdbd and MariaDB. node_id defaults to the controller node. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--accounting))
- `allow_controller_host` (Boolean) Let the controller node also be a compute member.
- `backup_controller` (Block List, Max: 1) Optional second slurmctld node. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--backup_controller))
- `cluster_name` (String) Slurm ClusterName. Defaults to name.
- `extra_config` (String) Lines appended to slurm.conf.
- `force` (Boolean) Pass force when deleting. Rows are dropped even when a member is unreachable, and the units are not removed from it.
- `gpu_driver` (Boolean) Install the host NVIDIA driver on compute members. gres = "auto" needs it.
- `login_node_ids` (List of String) Nodes that get the login role. They may also host guests.
- `storage` (Block List, Max: 1) Shared storage. With mode nfs the controller node exports the paths, which makes it a single point of failure for them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--storage))
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `user` (Block List) Cluster users. The uid is fixed so it matches on every member. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--user))
- `wait_for_ready` (Boolean) Wait until the reconciler reports the cluster ready before apply returns.

### Read-Only

- `generation` (Number)
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `node_status` (List of Object) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--node_status))
- `phase` (String) pending, applying, ready, degraded, deleting, or failed.
- `status_message` (String)

<a id="nestedblock--compute"></a>
### Nested Schema for `compute`

Required:

- `address` (String) Management address other members use to reach this node.
- `iface` (String) Management interface, for example enp6s0.
- `node_id` (String) kcore node id.

Optional:

- `gres` (String) none or auto. auto reports the node's GPUs to Slurm and needs gpu_driver = true.
- `partitions` (List of String) Partitions this node serves. Each must be declared in a partition block.
- `reserve_cores` (Number) Cores held back from jobs for the host.
- `reserve_memory_mb` (Number) Memory in MiB held back from jobs for the host.

Required:

- `address` (String) Management address other members use to reach this node.
- `iface` (String) Management interface, for example enp6s0.
- `node_id` (String) kcore node id.

- `state` (String) For example UP.
